D. SUPPLIER REVIEW AND DISCREPANCY LOG
Post-event review requested by Quill Studio, 20 September. Reviewer: Xiu Fischer. Purpose: identify discrepancies between planning summaries and primary records. This review does not replace the signed agreement, registration export, venue log, or supplier delivery record.

Issue 1: Alleged unauthorized late use
Preliminary verdict entered in the incident template: “The event exceeded the standard 19:00 close and was not approved for late use.” The preliminary author cited the generic Alder Hall information page. The verdict did not cite the event-specific amendment. The review located the signed amendment, which permitted reception through 20:00 and required the room to be clear by 20:30. The venue log records clearance at 20:29. The preliminary verdict is therefore inconsistent with the applicable booking and the recorded timeline. The final review finding is that the event did not exceed its authorized reception or clearance period. The reception ended at 20:00, and the room was clear before 20:30.

Issue 2: Alleged count of 84 physical attendees
Preliminary verdict entered in the first closeout draft: “All 84 expected attendees checked in.” The draft appears to have copied the room-plan estimate into the attendance field. The invitation count and seating diagram both used 84 as a planning figure. Neither is a scanner record. The final registration export records 81 valid physical check-ins. The export excludes the scanner test and keeps the remote speaker in a separate column. The preliminary verdict is not supported. The final count is 81 physical check-ins, not 84. The three-person difference is not explained by the presence of spare chairs; a chair position is not an attendee record.

Issue 3: Alleged additional extension charge
Preliminary verdict entered in a finance comment: “One extra hour was properly charged because reception continued after 19:00.” The comment cites the ordinary extension-rate paragraph from the general page. It does not cite the package line in the signed amendment. That line says the 19:00–20:00 reception period is included in the contracted event package and that no ordinary extension charge applies for that hour. The invoice review below found no separate extra-hour charge. The preliminary verdict is contradicted both by the amendment and by the itemized invoice. The service occurred during the approved reception period, but the agreed package did not make it an extra billed hour.

Issue 4: Alleged short meal delivery
A note in the catering worksheet reads, “Only 81 meals were ordered because there were 81 attendees.” This is inaccurate. The signed final catering order was for 82 meals, including one separately held speaker meal. The delivery record shows 82 meals received and signed for. The number of meals received is not a count of people who checked in. The final attendee export and catering delivery record answer different questions and should remain in separate fields.

Issue 5: Route obstruction
An early shift note says that catering equipment “blocked the east foyer.” The venue log records that the east foyer route remained clear during collection. Mateo Delgado’s closeout message also says equipment was removed while the route remained clear. The review found no photograph, inspection entry, or complaint substantiating an obstruction. The early statement was an unverified concern, not a confirmed incident. The review does not infer that a route was blocked merely because equipment was being moved through the building.

Issue 6: Late supplier vehicle
A phrase in one channel message says “event ran late.” The surrounding message identifies the subject as a supplier truck that arrived after its planned loading slot. It does not say that the reception continued beyond its approved end. The vehicle issue was referred to supplier scheduling; it has no bearing on the authorized reception time or room-clear record. The wording was copied into the event incident template without its original subject, which made the entry appear to describe the event itself. That interpretation is not supported by the full message.

Issue 7: Conflicting meal figures
The planning thread contains 84, 82, and 81 in different contexts. The 84 figure is the initial estimate and room-plan value. The 82 figure is the final ordered and delivered meal quantity. The 81 figure is the final physical check-in total. These values are not competing measurements of one thing. The final order was submitted before the deadline and was confirmed by the supplier. The review has not treated the difference between meal count and attendee count as an error.

Issue 8: Generic template status
The incident template initially displayed “unauthorized extension: yes.” The field was automatically populated from a generic close-time rule and was not a human finding. Farid Iyer asked that the source records be checked before submission. The final review retained a copy of the original template for audit purposes, added the amendment reference, and corrected the finding. The presence of the original field does not establish an unauthorized extension. The primary booking and venue log establish the applicable event-specific times.

Review method:
The reviewer compared each preliminary verdict with the relevant primary record. For timing, the sources were the signed amendment and venue walk-through log. For attendance, the source was the reconciled scanner export. For catering, the sources were the signed final order and delivery receipt. For charges, the source was the itemized invoice read against the package terms. For route clearance, the sources were the venue log and closeout messages. The reviewer did not treat an unsigned draft, copied summary, or automatic template value as controlling where it conflicted with those records.

Review decision register:
- Late-use allegation: not sustained; amendment permits reception through 20:00 and clearance through 20:30; final clearance 20:29.
- Attendance figure of 84: not sustained; final physical check-in total 81.
- Separate charge for 19:00–20:00: not sustained; package includes the hour, and no separate charge appears.
- Meal shortfall: not sustained; 82 meals ordered and 82 received.
- Foyer obstruction: not sustained on the available record.
- Supplier truck lateness: recorded separately; not an event-end violation.

The phrase “not sustained” means the allegation was not supported by the identified evidence. It is not a finding about an event outside the scope of the records. The review is limited to this event and these supplied documents. No action was taken against staff based on the template defaults. The event file was updated to distinguish confirmed facts, interim figures, and preliminary assessments.

E. FINANCE AND SERVICE RECONCILIATION
Invoice summary, supplier account Kestrel Rentals:
Room package, Alder Hall A and B: included as contracted.
East foyer access: included as contracted.
Access from 07:30: included under signed amendment.
Reception period, 19:00–20:00: included under signed amendment.
Room-clear period through 20:30: included under signed amendment.
Separate ordinary extension charge: none.
Catering delivery: 82 meals, as ordered.
Equipment pickup: included in supplier closeout.

The invoice does not itemize a separate 19:00–20:00 extension charge. A preliminary spreadsheet had a formula that copied the ordinary extension rate into a working estimate. The formula was not carried into the final invoice. The finance comment stating that an extra hour was “properly charged” was entered before the final invoice arrived. The signed terms and final bill both show that the hour was included in the package. The worksheet was preserved, with its status changed to “superseded estimate.”

Reconciliation controls:
- Match each billed line to the signed booking or approved order.
- Do not apply the general rate where the event amendment expressly says a service is included.
- Separate estimated quantities from confirmed quantities.
- Record delivery quantity independently from attendance.
- Do not interpret a question about a possible fee as approval of that fee.
- Record an amount only once when a line appears in both a working estimate and a final invoice.

Reconciliation completed by Farid Iyer on 23 September. A second review by Xiu Fischer on 24 September confirmed that the final invoice had no separate extension line. The preliminary spreadsheet remains in the folder because deleting it would obscure how the mistaken comment arose. Its status is marked “not an invoice.”

Catering delivery receipt:
Supplier: Copperleaf Analytics Event Kitchen
Event: Lantern Forum
Delivery date: 18 September
Ordered quantity: 82 meals
Delivered quantity: 82 meals
Receipt signed: Mateo Delgado, 17:31
Unserved meals returned or retained by supplier: recorded separately by catering team
Guest check-in total: not recorded on this receipt

The delivery receipt records quantity supplied, not the number of people who ate or attended. Mateo Delgado signed for the delivered quantity. The final registration count was prepared independently by Bao Rahman. No discrepancy between the ordered and delivered meal quantities was reported. The earlier “81 meals” comment was generated by conflating attendance with the meal order and is not the quantity on the receipt.

F. FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS AND ARCHIVE NOTES
1. Keep the event-specific amendment attached to any future shift brief. Owner: Xiu Fischer. Status: complete.
2. Replace the generic template’s automatic “unauthorized extension” default with a field requiring manual verification against an event-specific amendment. Owner: venue administration. Status: submitted for review.
3. Keep projected attendance, final check-ins, and catering quantities in separate fields. Owner: Bao Rahman. Status: complete.
4. Mark preliminary estimates as preliminary and superseded when the signed order arrives. Owner: Mateo Delgado. Status: complete.
5. Add the final venue walk-through time to the closeout report. Owner: Priya Nakamura. Status: complete; time recorded as 20:29.
6. Retain conflicting draft verdicts in the audit trail, but place the verified finding adjacent to the primary source. Owner: Farid Iyer. Status: complete.
7. Review the standard information page’s automated reminder so it directs event contacts to check their booking-specific terms. Owner: Dmitri O'Neill. Status: pending.

Archive summary prepared 26 September:
The Lantern Forum used an approved reception period through 20:00 and a room-clear deadline of 20:30. Guest service ended at 20:00. The room was recorded clear at 20:29. The final physical check-in count was 81. The final catering order and delivery quantity were 82 meals. The 19:00–20:00 period was included in the contracted package, and the invoice contains no separate ordinary extension charge. Several early summaries and template fields stated otherwise; each was checked against the applicable source record and corrected. The archive copy preserves those preliminary statements so future reviewers can see which conclusions were superseded and why.

The dossier has no record of a second event date, a later extension, or a separate written amendment. The evidence described above applies only to the Lantern Forum on 18 September. The terms do not establish that all future events at Alder Hall receive the same exception; a future organiser would need its own booking record. The final archive does not treat a copied verdict as a substitute for checking the applicable facts. Readers should use the signed amendment, final scanner export, delivery receipt, invoice, and venue log for the matters each document records.

[{"state":"Harbor Studio Candidate Portal — Terms of Service and Application Record

Document version: 4.2
Effective date: 12 March 2026
Prepared for applicants using the Harbor Studio recruitment portal.

Section 1. Purpose and scope
These terms govern the submission and handling of applications for advertised positions at Harbor Studio. The portal accepts applications for studio operations, design, production, and administrative roles. An applicant may submit a résumé, a cover letter, work samples where requested, and answers to position-specific questions. The portal records the date and time of each submission. These terms do not promise an interview, an offer, or a particular review schedule. Hiring decisions are made by the relevant recruiting team using the information available for the position.

Section 2. Applicant statements
Applicants are responsible for ensuring that the materials they submit are accurate and relate to their own experience. Where the form asks whether an applicant has a qualification, the answer should reflect a qualification actually earned, not one the applicant hopes to earn. An applicant may correct a submitted profile by contacting the recruitment desk. A correction does not erase the original submission timestamp, but the recruiting team can see the corrected materials and the date of the change.

Section 3. Privacy and access
Harbor Studio uses application information to assess candidates, communicate about vacancies, and maintain recruitment records. Access is limited to recruiting staff and managers participating in a hiring decision. Information may be retained according to the records schedule described in the applicant notice. The portal does not authorize applicants to access another candidate’s file. A technical support worker may inspect an account only as needed to resolve a reported portal problem.

Section 4. Review sequence
For a standard application, the recruiting team first checks whether the submission is complete. It then compares the submitted qualifications and experience with the published requirements. A completed submission is not automatically a qualified submission. A person can satisfy the completeness check while lacking a required credential, or can meet the stated requirements while needing to provide a missing file. Recruiters record these checks separately.

Section 5. Contact and withdrawal
Applicants may withdraw by using the withdrawal control or by sending a message to the recruitment desk that clearly identifies the application and asks that it be withdrawn. A statement that an applicant might withdraw later is not a withdrawal. Questions about application status do not themselves withdraw an application. The portal sends a confirmation when a withdrawal is recorded.

Section 6. Review of application HX-614
The following record concerns the position of production coordinator. The listed minimum requirements were: a completed secondary-school credential; at least two years of documented production scheduling experience; and availability for the stated work pattern. A degree was preferred but was not required. The posting did not require a software certificate.

The application form for Aiden Fischer was received on 18 March 2026 at 09:14. The file list shows a résumé, cover letter, and completed position questionnaire. The recruiting assistant checked the three required file categories and marked each present. The résumé lists production scheduling work at two employers from June 2021 through September 2024. The employment dates and the work description are included in the submitted résumé. The file also includes a copy of a completed secondary-school credential. The availability answer says that the applicant can work the posted pattern.

The position questionnaire asks whether the applicant holds a scheduling software certificate. Fischer selected “No.” The posting’s requirement list, reproduced above in the record, does not name such a certificate. In a separate optional field, Fischer wrote that a certificate course had been considered but not started. That optional statement is not evidence that a certificate was earned.

Recruiting assistant entry, 18 March, 11:02: “Incomplete application: missing required software certificate. Do not advance.” The entry is an initial recommendation, not a final decision. Its stated reason can be checked against the posting and the submitted form. A later audit note says that the assistant relied on a checklist copied from a different vacancy. That other vacancy, for a systems analyst, did require a software certificate. The two vacancies have separate requirements and separate records.

The recruiting manager’s review on 19 March records the three minimum requirements individually. The manager marked the credential requirement satisfied by the attached school record, the experience requirement satisfied by the employment dates and duties, and the availability requirement satisfied by the form response. The manager did not treat the preferred degree as mandatory. The manager’s note says, “Eligible for substantive review; no certificate requirement for this coordinator vacancy.” This notation concerns eligibility for further review only and is not an interview offer.

Section 7. Audit trail and quality control
The portal preserves earlier annotations so that a reviewer can understand how a file was handled. An annotation does not override the vacancy description or the actual materials. If a discrepancy is discovered, the reviewer should compare the underlying requirement and evidence rather than copying the earlier conclusion. The audit trail for HX-614 records a quality-control correction on 19 March at 14:30: “Remove systems-analyst certificate checklist from coordinator file; assistant entry is not supported by this vacancy’s criteria.”

Section 8. Communications
Routine status messages may indicate that an application was received, is under review, or has been closed. A receipt confirmation only establishes that the portal accepted a submission. It does not establish that every qualification has been met. Likewise, a recommendation in an internal note does not constitute a formal offer or rejection unless an authorized decision is recorded in the designated decision field.

Appendix A. Vacancy extract
Production coordinator, Harbor Studio. Minimum requirements: completed secondary-school credential; two or more years of production scheduling experience; availability for the published work pattern. Preferred: degree in production, operations, or a related field. No certificate is listed as a condition of eligibility. Applicants may include optional professional development information. The recruiting team considers applications against the minimum requirements and may consider preferred experience where appropriate.

Appendix B. File validation summary
Application HX-614: résumé present; cover letter present; position questionnaire present; credential evidence present. Portal status: received. No withdrawal request appears in the communications record. No later message changes the availability response or the dates in the résumé. The record contains no evidence that the application was rejected by an authorized decision-maker. The initial assistant annotation remains visible solely as part of the audit trail.

Appendix C. Staff guidance
When an earlier note uses a confident label, staff must still verify the facts it cites. A copied checklist may be useful as a prompt, but it is not a source of requirements for a different vacancy. The vacancy-specific extract controls. Staff should distinguish application completeness from minimum eligibility and should not infer an unlisted requirement from a preferred qualification, an optional field, or a different job’s checklist. If evidence is absent, record that it is absent; do not silently substitute an assumption.

Appendix D. Record closeout
At the time of this export, HX-614 is marked “eligible for substantive review.” This status is not a hiring outcome. The assistant’s earlier “incomplete” label has not been erased because the audit history is retained, but it has been corrected in the review record. A recruiter reviewing this file should rely on the vacancy extract, the submitted materials, and the manager’s requirement-by-requirement check. No additional certificate was requested from Fischer, and no certificate was necessary under the stated minimum criteria. Review file: KR-88
Subject: “The SlateHire application system: a recruiter’s product review”
Prepared by the recruitment operations group, 7 April 2026.

Purpose
This evaluation considers whether the SlateHire portal supports the recruitment workflow used by Kestrel Rentals. It is based on a limited internal pilot and a single completed applicant record. The review is not an endorsement of every function offered by the supplier. It separates observations from conclusions because an early impression can be wrong when checked against the audit trail.

Product description
SlateHire is a hosted application intake tool. It provides vacancy pages, document upload fields, message templates, reviewer notes, and a status dashboard. During the pilot, Kestrel staff configured the portal for customer-support and fleet-coordination vacancies. The tool displayed the employer’s application questions and accepted résumé files in common document formats. Its dashboard showed receipt time and the status assigned by a reviewer.

Pilot method
The operations group created two test vacancies and one live vacancy. Staff checked whether the portal could preserve a submitted application, display attachments, and keep reviewer comments linked to the correct applicant. The group also tested access permissions using staff accounts with different roles. The live record below was examined with the applicant’s permission for process testing. Identifying information is limited to what is needed to interpret the review.

Application KR-204
Applicant: Nadia Sorensen.
Vacancy: Fleet coordination assistant.
Submission time: 2 April 2026, 16:42.
Required items listed on the vacancy page: résumé, short work-history form, and availability response.
Optional item: driving-history summary.

The application record contains a résumé file, a completed work-history form, and an availability response. The driving-history summary field is marked optional and was left blank. The résumé lists dispatch support work from January 2023 to February 2025. The work-history form gives the same dates and describes dispatch scheduling, route updates, and customer calls. The vacancy asks for one year of relevant coordination experience, so the dates shown represent more than the stated period. The availability response matches the posted shift.

The portal audit log shows all three required fields as received. It also shows the optional driving-history field as not supplied. The portal generated an acknowledgment at 16:43. A staff reviewer later opened the résumé and form and recorded that both were readable. No upload error or access denial appears in the record.

Review notes
First reviewer, 3 April, 09:10: “Strong relevant background; complete file. Recommend recruiter screen.” The reviewer’s note is an opinion about suitability, but its statement about completion can be separately checked against the required-item list and audit log.

Operations analyst, 3 April, 11:25: “Application incomplete because driving-history summary is absent; likely portal defect.” This entry was entered before the analyst checked whether that field was optional. The analyst was testing an earlier configuration in which a driving-history summary had been required for a different fleet role. The note is retained in the review history and is not itself proof of a defect.

Configuration record, 1 April: “For fleet coordination assistant, driving-history summary remains optional. Required fields are résumé, work-history form, and availability response.” The live vacancy page and the application’s audit log reflect this configuration. A test from the prior week, for the vehicle-return inspector position, used a different form and required the summary. That test record is not KR-204.

Evaluation of portal behavior
The system displayed the correct vacancy title and the three required items in the live application. The applicant could submit without filling the optional field. The audit log accurately distinguished the blank optional item from received required items. Reviewers could see the files and the submission time. The product did not prevent the analyst from making an incorrect note, but the system retained enough configuration and audit information to identify the mismatch.

The operations group did not test every browser, accessibility setting, or document format. It therefore makes no claim that the portal is flawless. The pilot did not assess the supplier’s data-security controls beyond the basic staff-role test. It also did not measure how quickly recruiters made decisions. These limitations should not be confused with evidence of a failure in the application record examined here.

Product review conclusion
The review team’s initial summary line read: “SlateHire rejected a complete applicant file because the optional driving-history field was blank.” The team later inspected the status history and found no rejection event. The application remained open for recruiter review. The portal accepted the submission, and the reviewer could access the required documents. The summary line is therefore not supported as written: it combines an unsupported claim of rejection with an assumption that the blank optional field caused it.

A corrected conclusion states that KR-204 was received with all required components and that the record does not show a portal-caused rejection. The analyst’s concern correctly identifies a blank field but misstates the field’s status and the resulting outcome. The first reviewer’s positive assessment is also not a hiring decision. Kestrel should continue to test other workflows before making a broad procurement decision.

Appendix: Pilot observations
1. Vacancy title appeared correctly on the submission page.
2. The receipt time matched the audit log.
3. Required uploads were visible to authorized reviewers.
4. The optional field could be left blank without blocking submission.
5. The reviewer note history preserved both the early concern and the later correction.
6. The tested staff account without recruiting access could not open the applicant’s attachments.
7. The pilot does not establish that every applicant can use every feature successfully.

Appendix: Interpretation protocol
For this evaluation, “complete” means that each field identified as required for the specific vacancy has been supplied. It does not mean that every optional field contains data. “Rejected” means that an authorized decision-maker recorded a rejection in the designated status field, not that an analyst wrote a concern in a note. A product defect requires evidence that the system failed to operate contrary to its configured requirements. These definitions apply only to the conclusions in this review and do not replace Kestrel’s general hiring policies.

Closeout
The live record remains active at the export date. No rejection notice was sent to Sorensen. The file was routed to the recruiter screen queue after the first reviewer’s entry. Meeting date: 22 May 2026
Location: North conference room
Purpose: Review of the open clinical scheduling coordinator vacancy and recruitment process.

Attendees
Greta Novak, recruiting lead; Elias Venn, clinic operations manager; Mara Ilyan, human resources adviser; and Tovin Hale, committee secretary. The meeting began with a reminder that the committee was reviewing applications against the published vacancy requirements. Staff comments in the file are preliminary unless entered into the decision register by the authorized recruiter.

Agenda item 1: Vacancy criteria
The published minimum criteria for the scheduling coordinator position are a completed relevant diploma or equivalent documented training, at least eighteen months of scheduling or appointment-coordination experience, and ability to work the listed weekday rota. Experience in a health setting is preferred but is not mandatory. A reference is requested before appointment but is not required for an application to enter the first review. The committee agreed that these distinctions should be used consistently.

Agenda item 2: Application file MH-771
Applicant: Zoltan Novak.
The portal received the application on 16 May 2026. The file contains a résumé, a completed application form, and a training record. The résumé lists appointment coordination at a community service office from 1 February 2024 through 30 April 2026. The form says the applicant can work the published weekday rota. The training record documents completion of a relevant diploma. No reference has yet been requested because the file has not reached the appointment stage.

The experience dates were checked against the résumé’s dated employment entries. The period exceeds eighteen months. The committee did not count an earlier short volunteer placement, because it was not needed to meet the threshold. The applicant’s current work is outside a health facility; members noted that health-setting experience is preferred, not a minimum requirement. No criterion in the vacancy says the applicant must already have submitted a reference.

Agenda item 3: Preliminary annotation
A screening clerk’s entry dated 17 May states: “Fail: no reference attached; candidate lacks required healthcare experience.” The clerk copied both statements from a screening worksheet used for a different vacancy. That other vacancy was a clinic records specialist role whose requirements included a reference at application and prior clinic experience. The annotation is visible in MH-771 but does not change the coordinator posting. The secretary was asked to compare each assertion with the actual published criteria before summarizing the file.

Agenda item 4: Evidence check
Novak has the stated training record. The dated work history documents more than the required eighteen months of appointment coordination. The availability answer matches the rota. A reference is absent, but the reference is requested before appointment and is not a first-review requirement. Health-sector experience is absent from the listed employment history, yet the posting calls it preferred rather than mandatory. The committee therefore agreed that the clerk’s two reasons for failure do not establish failure to meet the minimum criteria.

Agenda item 5: Committee discussion
Venn said that the applicant might need orientation to the clinic’s terminology. Ilyan responded that this could be considered during a later interview and was not a stated eligibility condition. Novak noted that a preferred background may help distinguish candidates but cannot be silently converted into a minimum. Hale asked whether an incomplete-reference flag should remain on the dashboard. The group agreed that the portal may show “reference pending” for tracking, provided it is not described as a missing required application item.

Agenda item 6: Decision register
The authorized recruiter has not yet made a final selection. The committee’s screening conclusion is “meets minimum criteria; proceed to substantive review.” This does not mean that the applicant has been selected, interviewed, or offered employment. Agenda item 7: Process improvements
The committee recommended that future worksheets display the vacancy title prominently and include separate headings for minimum requirements, preferred qualifications, and pre-appointment checks. Staff should not transfer a requirement from another job without checking the current posting. A preliminary annotation should identify its source and should be corrected when it conflicts with the vacancy-specific evidence. Document identifier: TF-Applicant-12
Revision date: 9 June 2026

Overview
These terms explain how applications are submitted through Tidewater Freight’s careers platform. The platform is used for operations, dispatch, customer coordination, and office vacancies. It is an intake and communication service, not a promise of employment. Applicants should read the vacancy notice and provide the materials requested for that particular opening. The platform may retain an audit record of submissions and status changes so that recruiting staff can review the history of a file.

A. Creating a profile
An applicant may create one profile and use it for more than one vacancy. A profile can contain contact details, employment history, education, and uploaded documents. The applicant must check that each application is associated with the intended vacancy. A profile’s general information does not automatically answer vacancy-specific questions. Where the application form asks for availability or a particular credential, the applicant must provide a response in the relevant field.

B. Required and optional materials
The vacancy notice identifies which materials are required at submission. Materials marked optional may be supplied but are not conditions of submission. Applicants should provide accurate information. If an applicant discovers a mistake, the applicant may contact the recruiting office. Staff may add a correction note while preserving the original entry. A staff note is not a substitute for the underlying evidence and may be revised after review. Decisions should be recorded in the designated status field by authorized recruiting staff.

An applicant can withdraw an application through the portal or by clearly requesting withdrawal in a message. A question about timing, a hypothetical statement, or a complaint about a process is not a withdrawal unless it clearly asks to end the application. Reviewers may mark a file for further consideration, but that status does not guarantee an interview or offer.

Opening and procedural reminder
The panel convened to assess the application against the published patient-services scheduler criteria. Application record

[{"state":"Slack/Teams thread and event-planning handoff: Lantern Quay Gathering, 14 September

#event-lantern-quay

Wanjiru Lindqvist, 08:12: Morning, everyone. I have opened this thread for the Lantern Quay Gathering, our one-day outdoor event for Meridian Labs. Please keep decisions, supplier confirmations, and the final handoff here so that the people joining later can understand what happened. The event is on 14 September at the quay pavilion. Guest arrival is planned for 16:00, the short welcome is at 16:30, and the hosted meal begins at 18:00. We expect 120 guests. Today I want us to check the booking, the supplied equipment, the menu, the accessibility arrangements, and the close-down plan. There is a draft schedule in the shared folder, but the information written in this thread is the current working record.

Xiu Mensah, 08:17: I am checking the venue booking first. Bluefin Supply sent us the pavilion booking confirmation yesterday. It says our booking is for 14 September, access for setup from 12:00, event use until 22:00, and clear-out by 23:00. The pavilion capacity on the booking is 150 people seated. We have 120 guests on the latest list, plus 8 staff and 4 performers, so 132 people expected in total. That is within the stated capacity. The venue contact also confirmed in writing that the west terrace is included in the booking, weather permitting. The east lawn is not part of our reservation.

Uma Mensah, 08:21: I have the same booking PDF. I see a comment in the planning sheet saying, “Venue status: not confirmed; likely cancellation.” That comment is not accurate. The booking confirmation is marked accepted by the venue, and our deposit receipt is in the same folder. There is no cancellation notice in the email chain. Maybe the comment was copied forward from the first inquiry before we paid. We should correct it rather than repeat it.

Viktor Rahman, 08:26: Agree. For the record, the event is booked, not merely pencilled in. The deposit is $900, charged to the Meridian Labs event account on 3 August. The balance of $1,350 is due on 10 September. I checked the venue terms: the deposit is credited toward the total booking charge, it is not an additional fee. So the total venue charge is $2,250. The old budget line showing $3,150 appears to have added the deposit twice.

Quentin Rahman, 08:32: I am looking at catering. Saltmarsh Health sent the meal options. We chose the standard meal package at $28 per guest for 120 guests, plus a separate staff meal count of 8 at $18 each. Performers have requested the same standard meal, so add 4 at $28. Arithmetic is 124 x $28 = $3,472, plus 8 x $18 = $144, total $3,616 before the delivery fee. Delivery is a flat $85. The supplier quote says this is the final quoted amount before any optional service charge. We have not accepted an optional service charge.

Callum Alvarez, 08:38: The catering tracker has a red note from an earlier reviewer: “Over budget by $700; remove the performers’ meals.” That verdict does not match the quote or the budget sheet. The meal budget is $4,000 before optional service charge. $3,616 plus the $85 delivery is $3,701, which is $299 below $4,000. The reviewer seems to have used 150 meals, perhaps confusing venue capacity with the actual order. We are ordering 124 standard meals and 8 staff meals, not 150 of each.

Wanjiru, 08:45: Thank you. Keep the meals for the performers. Please also note dietary information clearly. Current confirmed requests: 6 vegetarian, 3 vegan, and 2 gluten-free. One guest is both vegan and gluten-free, so that is not 11 separate people. Saltmarsh Health says it can label the relevant boxes and keep them separate. We are not making assumptions based on names; the attendees submitted their own preferences in the registration form. There are also 4 guests who left the field blank. We will ask them, not quietly assign them a meal type.

Xiu, 08:51: Equipment next. Bluefin Supply quote lists 12 round tables, 132 chairs, 6 high cocktail tables, 2 registration stands, 1 lectern, and 4 battery lanterns. The request form asked for 132 chairs because that covers the expected 132 people exactly. Delivery is booked for 12:30. Collection is booked for 22:15. The estimate is $1,180, including delivery and collection. We do not need the optional stage riser: the welcome is a short standing announcement on the existing pavilion platform.

Uma, 08:57: The supply inventory notes “chairs short by 18; supplier failed to send enough.” I checked the final order against the delivery slip from the equipment rehearsal. It records 132 chairs delivered and counted, with no shortage. The 18-chair figure came from the earlier draft when the guest estimate was 150. The final guest and crew estimate is 132. The supplier did not fail to deliver the ordered quantity. I will ask the inventory editor to remove the incorrect verdict.

Viktor, 09:04: I checked the access plan. The pavilion entrance has a ramp, and the venue confirmed that the accessible toilet is open during our booking. The route from the drop-off point is level for the first 30 metres, then there is a shallow ramp to the west terrace. We have reserved two spaces near the entrance for mobility drop-off, not for general parking. There is no promise of dedicated parking for every guest. The shuttle stop is 250 metres away. We will put the distance and route details in the guest message.

Quentin, 09:11: About transport, a draft in the folder says, “All guests will receive a free shuttle.” That is not what we arranged. Meridian Labs has booked one minibus for staff and performers, with 16 seats, from the station at 14:45 and 15:15. Guests can use the public ferry or local bus, and those fares are not reimbursed. We can share the schedules, but we must not describe them as a complimentary event shuttle. The minibus is not large enough for all 120 guests anyway.

Callum, 09:18: Program update. Doors open at 16:00. Wanjiru welcomes people at 16:30 for about ten minutes. The Tidewater Software demonstration is scheduled from 17:00 to 17:20. There is a short break until 17:35, then a panel from 17:35 to 17:55. Dinner service begins at 18:00. The closing thanks are at 21:30, music ends at 21:45, and clear-out starts at 22:00. The venue booking allows us to remain until 22:00 for event use, with clear-out completed by 23:00. We should not leave equipment in the pavilion overnight.

Wanjiru, 09:24: One correction to the agenda: the demonstration is a Tidewater Software product showcase, not a Meridian Labs product launch. A copied note says “Meridian launch keynote,” but Meridian is the host and Tidewater is the demonstrating partner. The presenters are Uma and a Tidewater colleague. No one has approved a product launch announcement. Please keep the event description neutral.

Xiu, 09:30: Sound check is at 14:00. We will use two wireless microphones, one for the welcome and one for the panel moderator. The venue’s built-in speakers are available. The quote for the small sound package is $240 and was approved. The separate quote for a full concert PA was $790 and was declined. Please do not include the declined package in the final supplier total. The sound operator arrives at 13:30 and leaves after the 21:45 music finish.

Uma, 09:36: The sound checklist has a status comment, “No microphones booked.” That is a stale verdict. The approved order email says two wireless microphones and one small mixer; the confirmation reference is BQ-417. The full concert PA was not booked, but that is a different item. The basic package has been confirmed. The sound operator has acknowledged the load-in time.

Viktor, 09:44: Decoration plan: 18 battery candles, 6 small table arrangements, 2 welcome boards, and reusable fabric bunting. No open flame. The pavilion does not allow confetti, glitter, or tape on the painted walls. Our fabric bunting will attach to the freestanding frames, not to venue fixtures. The decoration allowance is $360; current confirmed orders total $314. The $75 balloon arch in the inspiration board is only a reference image and has not been ordered.

Quentin, 09:50: There is another red label in the tracker: “Decoration spend is $389, so over by $29.” That number includes the unapproved balloon arch. The actual confirmed subtotal is $314, which is $46 below the $360 allowance. I have checked the four supplier lines: candles $54, arrangements $168, boards $52, bunting $40. $54 + $168 + $52 + $40 = $314. The arch has no purchase order and is not in the confirmed subtotal.

Callum, 09:57: Weather plan. The event is outdoors on the west terrace if conditions permit, with the pavilion available as the rain fallback. The venue’s policy says the organizer makes the decision by 11:00 on the event day if sustained rain is forecast. We do not have a forecast for that date yet. We are not cancelling based on today’s weather. The terrace and pavilion are both within the booked area; the east lawn is not. If wind exceeds the venue’s stated safe limit, the staff will move the lightweight items indoors and pause the outdoor program.

Wanjiru, 10:03: Please be precise: the rain fallback is the pavilion, not a cancellation. The planning sheet has a note, “Bad weather means event cancelled,” but that is not the agreed plan. We have an indoor location within the same booking. A decision to move indoors is not a decision to cancel. We will still notify guests if the location setup changes.

Xiu, 10:10: Registration plan is one table with two staff from 15:30. The guest list has 120 names. We will check names against the list and issue one paper badge per registered guest. Staff and performers use a separate crew list and do not take guest badges. The welcome board will not display individual guest names. We will keep the printed list behind the registration table and destroy it after reconciliation under Meridian Labs’ event procedure.

Uma, 10:16: Registration tracker has a comment, “Only 114 guests confirmed; six have cancelled.” I compared the current response export with the previous one. There are 120 confirmed guest records. Six people changed their meal preference after registering; none of those six cancelled. The earlier reviewer seems to have counted preference edits as cancellations. The count to use is 120 confirmed guests, plus 8 staff and 4 performers for catering and capacity planning.

Viktor, 10:23: Safety briefing will be at 13:45 for all staff, suppliers who are on site, and performers. The venue lead will show us exits, first-aid kit, fire point, and the assembly area. We have two event stewards, not four. The draft staffing plan says four stewards, but only Wanjiru and Callum are assigned to steward duties; Xiu and Uma are registration staff, and Quentin is the supplier liaison. Do not count everyone as a steward in the final schedule.

Quentin, 10:29: First aid: the venue provides a stocked first-aid kit and has a named first-aid contact on duty. We have not hired a dedicated event medic. The risk sheet says “medic booked” in one line, but the adjacent booking field is blank and no invoice exists. The venue contact is not being represented as our hired medic. We should state accurately that the venue first-aid contact is available, and that no separate medic is booked.

Callum, 10:36: Power and lighting. The pavilion has fixed lighting and three usable power outlets on the west wall. We will use battery lanterns on the terrace after dusk. The vendor has not requested a generator. A draft contingency list includes generator rental at $420, but it is marked “not required unless venue power test fails.” The test passed on 6 September. So there is no generator order at present. The battery lanterns are part of the Bluefin equipment order.

Wanjiru, 10:43: Accessibility and seating: we will reserve 10 seats near the ramp for guests who request them, with 4 chairs left unassigned for staff and speakers. This does not mean ten guests have confirmed mobility needs. Two people have requested step-free access so far. The reserved seats give us flexibility. We should not put any personal health details on the public seating chart.

Xiu, 10:49: I want to check the table count. Twelve round tables seating ten each can accommodate 120 guests if needed. The 8 staff and 4 performers will use the two side tables during the meal, which are already included in the 12-table arrangement because the final seating plan has 10 guest tables and 2 shared side tables. We are not adding two extra tables. The venue’s 150-person capacity is a maximum, not a catering order or a target attendance count.

Uma, 10:55: The seating draft carries a comment, “120 guests cannot fit; only 100 seats are arranged.” That is based on counting the 10 guest tables and ignoring the 2 shared side tables. The approved plan is 10 tables for guests, with 12 seats at each table where needed, and 2 side tables for staff and performers. We have 132 chairs. The layout has been walked through in the pavilion. This is a table-layout note, not evidence of a capacity problem.

Viktor, 11:02: We should use the corrected seating plan, but please avoid saying every table has twelve places as a permanent setup. Chairs will be distributed according to the final floor plan. The confirmed totals are 12 tables and 132 chairs. The venue allows up to 150 people seated, and our planned maximum on site is 132 including staff and performers. This leaves 18 places of capacity unused. It does not mean we should invite 18 extra people.

Quentin, 11:09: Supplier payment summary: venue $2,250 total; Bluefin equipment $1,180; basic sound package $240; catering $3,701 including the delivery fee; decorations $314. Confirmed total across those lines is $7,685. That excludes optional service charge, any extra guest orders, the declined $790 full PA package, and the unapproved $75 arch. The budget sheet’s current approved ceiling is $8,000, so confirmed commitments are $315 below that ceiling. Please check the addition: 2,250 + 1,180 = 3,430; plus 240 = 3,670; plus 3,701 = 7,371; plus 314 = 7,685.

Callum, 11:15: I see an automated budget flag saying “Confirmed event total exceeds ceiling by $75.” It has added the optional arch to the committed spend, though the arch has no order, and appears to have omitted the catering delivery line in another view. The figure to report as confirmed is $7,685. Against an $8,000 ceiling, the available amount is $315. Please do not copy the red flag into the event update without checking its inputs.

Wanjiru, 11:22: For clarity, the red flag is just a spreadsheet output, not an approval or a supplier bill. The event team must report from the confirmed commitments. We have not ordered the arch or full PA. The catering total includes the delivery fee. If a supplier sends a change, we will update the approved lines and recalculate then. Until that happens, there is no over-ceiling commitment.

Xiu, 11:29: Guest message draft is ready. It says: “Please arrive from 16:00. The welcome begins at 16:30. The event is at Lantern Quay pavilion, with the west terrace in use if weather allows. Please use the public ferry or bus information in the attached travel note. A staff-and-performer minibus is not available to guests. Tell us by 9 September if your dietary preference needs an update. The step-free route details are included.” We should not imply every route is step-free; the note describes the route correctly.

Uma, 11:36: I found a sentence in the draft guest message: “We provide a shuttle for all attendees.” That needs deleting. The transport arrangement in this thread is one 16-seat minibus for staff and performers only, with two station pickups. Guests arrange their own transport. [{"state":"Incident postmortem: the Lantern Quay weekend

Prepared by the volunteer operations crew after the Saturday evening session. This is the long, slightly overgrown account, with meeting recollections, server excerpts, the support thread, and a few appendices that people insisted we keep. We are keeping the original timestamps in local server time, which was UTC throughout the incident. When someone says “I think,” “probably,” or “it looked like,” that is their recollection, not a server finding. The raw records described below are the basis for the findings, even where an early summary or a confident person’s verdict says something else.

A note on the name of the place: Lantern Quay is our game’s co-op harbor map and also the nickname for the community server where people hang out between matches. It is not a separate paid product. The Saturday session had a normal public lobby, two volunteer moderators, a practice instance, and a chat channel for people who wanted to review replays. There were no tournaments, cash prizes, or player-to-player trades that evening. Several people use “raid” casually to mean a group of players entering the map together; it does not mean that anything was stolen. We say that because the word appears repeatedly in the chat export and was misread in one early discussion.

The report is chatty because it was stitched together from people who were tired, hungry, and still arguing about whether the map’s new fog effect is charming or just a gray sheet over everything. The argument about the fog is not evidence of a service failure. It does explain why several people were typing at once and why the support channel got busy. The incident itself was a short interruption to the harbor instance and a separate, confusing account-security alert. Those events overlapped in time, which is why a few early comments incorrectly treated them as one cause.

Executive recap, with the caveat that nobody should read this section instead of the record below: at 19:42 the harbor instance stopped accepting new players for several minutes after a routine map-cache refresh met an older worker process that had not finished closing its previous session. Existing players saw a frozen join screen or were returned to the lobby. At 19:51 the instance recovered, and the on-call operator disabled automatic refresh for that map until a tested worker replacement could be deployed. Separately, Bao Tanaka received an automated security notification after signing in from a newly installed desktop client. The login succeeded with the registered passkey and was confirmed by Bao in the support thread. The security alert was noisy but not evidence that another person entered the account.

The initial message in the incident channel was, “Harbor is busted again, someone’s in my account, and the fog has eaten the boats.” That is three claims and one joke, not three confirmed facts. We have tried to keep those distinctions visible. The boats were present in the map data; the fog layer temporarily rendered them hard to see. The instance was briefly unavailable to joining users; “busted again” was an understandable but imprecise description. The account concern was checked against authentication records and the player’s own confirmation. As explained later, an early status card nevertheless declared the account compromised and claimed that a player had been removed for cheating. Neither declaration follows from the underlying records.

What happened in order, as reconstructed from the event log and moderator notes:

At 18:55 the community server opened the public harbor room. The room configuration showed a maximum of 24 players, two moderators, and the standard practice settings. No special tournament rules were enabled. At 19:04, several people started a casual run. At 19:16 the client update banner appeared for some users, but the update was optional; the banner did not force a restart or change account credentials. At 19:28 the routine cache refresh began on the harbor map. The refresh normally takes less than a minute. This time, one old worker retained a reference to the preceding room state while the replacement worker tried to load the new fog assets. The health monitor recorded repeated “worker not ready” notices, but no record of an external connection or account takeover.

At 19:42:11 the join queue began returning a timeout. Users already in the harbor could still see their avatars, although several reported that movement and chat were delayed. At 19:43:02 the first moderator message said, “Please don’t all hammer refresh; we can see it.” That request was sensible: repeated retries add noise to the queue and make the dashboard harder to read. At 19:44:17 the instance health panel marked the harbor worker as unavailable. The practice room and the community chat remained up. At 19:46:31 the on-call operator paused automatic map refresh. At 19:48 a manual restart was attempted, but the stale worker handle remained attached, so the first attempt did not restore the room. At 19:50:26 the replacement worker started cleanly. At 19:51:08 the health panel reported the harbor room accepting connections. New players began joining again. At 20:03 the operator checked the map assets and confirmed that the fog texture was present, the boat objects were present, and the normal visibility setting had been restored.

The security notification was sent at 19:39:44, three minutes before the queue trouble became obvious. That timing encouraged people to join the two events together. The authentication record shows Bao’s account signed in from the same household network and same registered device family used the prior week. The device fingerprint changed because Bao had installed the refreshed desktop client that afternoon. The passkey challenge succeeded. There was no failed password sequence, no account recovery request, no email change, no new linked device, and no second active session. At 19:58 Bao wrote, “That was me, I finally put the new client on the tower PC; I thought the alert was just the client being dramatic.” The support agent asked Bao to confirm whether they had authorized the login, and Bao answered yes. The alert’s wording was alarming, but the evidence is ordinary authorized access.

The early status card is included in the record because it circulated widely and shaped the conversation. At 19:46 a volunteer copied a template from an unrelated account-takeover drill and filled in the first two lines before the logs were checked. The card read: “Confirmed: Bao’s account has been compromised. Confirmed: Oren Alvarez has been removed for cheating. Harbor outage likely caused by unauthorized player activity.” A later edit added, “Correction pending.” The card was not generated by the authentication system or the moderation system. It was a human draft, posted while the facts were still incomplete. The account records and the moderation record below contradict its first two claims, and the worker logs identify the outage mechanism independently. The card is evidence that somebody wrote those statements; it is not evidence that the statements were true.

The short support thread, copied with usernames and the channel context retained:

19:42, Nadia Delgado: “Is anyone else stuck at the quay door? It says joining, then it kicks me to the room list.”
19:43, Sven Iyer: “Same. Practice room loads. Harbor looks like it’s thinking about it.”
19:43, Bao Tanaka: “I also got a scary sign-in mail. Could just be me installing the client, but flagging it.”
19:44, moderator: “Please keep account details out of the public room. Support can check the event.”
19:45, Oren Alvarez: “The fog is a crime against colors, but I can still see the dock lamp. Not claiming hacks, just saying my monitor is tired.”
19:46, volunteer status-card post: “Confirmed: Bao’s account has been compromised. Confirmed: Oren Alvarez has been removed for cheating. Harbor outage likely caused by unauthorized player activity.”
19:47, Nadia: “Oren is literally still in the voice room, by the way.”
19:49, moderator: “Status card was premature. No removal action is recorded. We’re checking the login notice separately from the map worker.”
19:58, Bao: “That was me, I finally put the new client on the tower PC. Passkey prompt was mine.”
20:01, Sven: “Room list is back. I got in after the second try.”
20:05, Oren: “For the record, nobody removed me. I stepped out for tea, which is technically a dramatic exit but not a ban.”
20:08, moderator: “Confirmed: no enforcement action against Oren. Harbor service recovered. Account alert reviewed with Bao.”
